name: JetBrains Air

form_factor.comment: Agentic development environment with a desktop IDE-like app for macOS, Linux, and Windows plus an organization-only web version for cloud tasks and automations. Per-form-factor links: IDE: https://air.dev/; Desktop App: https://www.jetbrains.com/help/air/quick-start-with-air.html; Web: https://air.jetbrains.cloud/.

released_in.comment: JetBrains launched Air as a public-preview agentic development environment in March 2026.

latest_major_update.comment: By September 10, 2026, Air documented desktop and organization web surfaces, JetBrains-managed cloud tasks and automations, organization repository connections, AI governance, and multiple built-in or ACP-compatible agents.

pricing.value: JetBrains AI Free, Pro, Ultimate, or organization credits; local tasks can use existing provider subscriptions or BYOK/API billing
pricing.comment: Air uses JetBrains AI credits for JetBrains-provided and cloud execution. Local desktop tasks can instead use connected Anthropic, OpenAI, or Google subscriptions or API billing, while user-added ACP agents retain their own metering.

some_free_usage.comment: JetBrains AI has a free tier with limited monthly credits; local Air tasks can also use separately free or locally hosted ACP-compatible agents where supported.

no_account_required.comment: The provider sign-in step can be skipped for an already installed ACP-compatible agent; JetBrains-managed, provider-subscription, web, and cloud use require their corresponding accounts.

can_use_other_subscriptions.comment: Local desktop tasks can use ChatGPT, Claude, Google, or API-billed provider accounts, and arbitrary locally installed ACP-compatible agents keep their own subscriptions.

rules.comment: Air recognizes project instruction files such as CLAUDE.md and AGENTS.md; exact agent-specific instruction behavior follows the selected harness.

skills.comment: Shared SKILL.md modules live under .agents/skills, with additional agent-specific skill directories for Claude Agent, Codex, Gemini CLI, and Junie.

hooks.comment: Air preserves agent-specific configuration behavior, but reviewed Air documentation does not expose a platform-wide lifecycle-hook API.

mcp_servers.comment: Settings can enable MCP, launch workspace MCP servers, and add global MCP server configurations.

custom_commands.comment: Air exposes built-in and custom commands in the slash menu alongside skills.

goal_command.comment: Tasks are goal-oriented, but no built-in persistent /goal command is documented for Air itself.

subagents.comment: Air runs several independent tasks in parallel and can launch a separate fresh-agent review task; subagent delegation inside a task depends on the selected agent harness.

monitor.comment: Cloud automations react to issue and repository events, schedules, and CI or delivery workflows without manual task starts.

transcripts.comment: Air retains task chats for continuation and review, but public documentation does not expose a portable local transcript format or path.

transcript_location.value: Task chats retained in-app; no portable local transcript path documented
transcript_location.comment: Air retains task chats for continuation and review, but public documentation does not expose a portable local transcript format or path.

model_selection.comment: Each new task selects an agent and model; the model can change within a task while its provider stays fixed.

approval_mode.comment: Per-task permission modes cover Plan, Ask, Edit, and Full Access, with names mapped to the selected agent's native behavior.

sandbox_mode.comment: Tasks can run in the local workspace, an isolated Git worktree, Docker, or a JetBrains-managed cloud environment.

resume.comment: Saved tasks can be reopened and continued from the Chat task history.

continue.comment: Follow-up messages continue the current task and can incorporate diff-review comments.

non_interactive.comment: Air exposes desktop and web user interfaces; no installable local headless Air command with verified prompt flags is documented.

output_format.comment: No Air-level JSON or structured-output mode is documented.

statusline.comment: Air has task controls and status in its UI, but no user-configurable CLI-style status line is documented.

telemetry.comment: Reviewed public settings documentation did not provide enough evidence for an Air-specific telemetry control.

keyboard_shortcuts.comment: Air documents keyboard shortcuts for changing modes, opening settings and actions, tools, and other editor workflows.

theme_customization.comment: Appearance settings include UI theme, editor color scheme, contrast, transparency, and interface scaling.

auto_save.comment: Reviewed public documentation did not expose a clear user-facing auto-save control.

debugging_output.comment: Reviewed public documentation did not expose a clear Air-level debug or verbose-output mode.

context_window.comment: Context limits follow the selected agent and model; no Air-level configurable token-window control is documented.

code_formatting.comment: Agents can run project tools in Air's terminal, but reviewed documentation did not establish a built-in configurable formatter integration.

git_integration.comment: Air can clone repositories, isolate tasks in worktrees or task branches, review diffs, generate commit messages, commit, push, and apply isolated changes locally.

performance_mode.comment: Reasoning effort and optional fast modes are selectable where the chosen agent supports them; there is no universal Air performance switch.

ui_customization.comment: Air exposes theme, color scheme, scaling, transparency, font, and tool-panel settings, but does not document arbitrary UI layout extensions.

hosted_agent.comment: JetBrains-managed cloud tasks clone the repository into isolated remote environments, run agents in parallel, commit and push task branches, and support web automations.

custom_model_provider.comment: Air connects first-party and external provider accounts and accepts arbitrary locally installed ACP-compatible agents, including agents backed by local models or custom providers.

notes: JetBrains Air is an agentic development environment and multi-harness surface, not a standalone local agent executable. It hosts Codex, Claude Agent, Gemini CLI, Junie, and user-added ACP agents, so no agent-launch backend was added.
